newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Bashneft Oil ordered to cease oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Russian Bashneft Oil ordered to cease oil exports.

text.p: The president of Russia's autonomous republic of Bashkiria has ordered the region's independent oil firm, Bashneft, to stop oil exports to leave more for refineries, Interfax news agency said on Wednesday.
Bashneft produced about 355,000 barrels a day in 1995, about six percent of Russia's total, and exported about 55,000 bpd, about three percent of Russia's total, according to Salomon Brothers.
It was not immediately clear whether Rakhimov could force Bashneft, a crude oil producer located in the Volga region, to cease exports.
Bashkiria President Murtaza Rakhimov was quoted as saying that more oil was needed for area refineries.
Bashneft said its crude oil output in 1996 was 326,880 bpd and that 1997 output would probably slip to 300,000 bpd.
It gave no figures for exports for those years.
The Fuel and Energy Ministry has in the past expressed concern that not enough crude oil is staying home for domestic refining.
